definition.def: If you describe something as marginal, you mean that it is small or not very important.
examples: This is a marginal improvement on October.
The role of the opposition party proved marginal.

definition.def: If you describe people as marginal, you mean that they are not involved in the main events or developments in society because they are poor or have no power.
examples: Andy Warhol made glamorous icons out of the most marginal people.
I don't want to call him marginal, but he's not a major character.

definition.def: In political elections, a marginal seat or constituency is one which is usually won or lost by only a few votes, and is therefore of great interest to politicians and journalists. [British]
examples: ...the views of voters in five marginal seats.

definition.def: Marginal activities, costs, or taxes are not the main part of a business or an economic system, but often make the difference between its success or failure, and are therefore important to control. [business]
examples: Consumer electronics has become a marginal business for the group.
For low-paid workers, the marginal tax rate is at least 75%.

definition.def: Marginal land is not very good for growing crops or grass for animals. [technical]
examples: ...helping farmers, so they do not have to exploit marginal lands.

examples.sentence: This attitude altered with the realisation that marginal communities can survive and adapt In spire of partial integration into a notoriously fickle world economy.
Unfortunately, the adaptations that enable carnivorous plants to thrive in marginal habitats also make them exquisitely sensitive.
